title: Introduce hybrid prefetch pipeline and cancel-path optimizations to reduce KV thrash and scheduler contention
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: In high-concurrency workloads we've observed KV cache hotkey thrash and increased scheduler contention when continuous-batching admission and prefetch compete with infrequently-cancelled long-running requests. This produces tail latency spikes and increases token cost due to repeated cache priming.

Goal: Implement a hybrid prefetch pipeline that separates speculative KV priming from admission-critical prefetch and introduce a lightweight cancel-path (delinquent-cancel) that fast-cancels speculative work without impacting commit/eviction semantics. Reduce global scheduler lock hold times by moving prefetch bookkeeping off the hot path and make eviction/refresh decisions event-driven rather than synchronous.

Scope:
- Introduce a speculative prefetch worker pool with backpressure tokens that can be dynamically sized per-tenant.
- Add a cancel-path signal that marks speculative tasks as cancellable, allowing fast-path reclamation of slot resources.
- Pull prefetch accounting out of the global slot allocator into a shadow-prefetch index with eventual consistency guarantees.
- Ensure KV cache invariants remain strongly consistent for committed sessions; speculative priming must never mutate commit-visible KV metadata.
- Lightweight metrics and tracing for prefetch lifecycle, cancel rates, reclaimed CPU/IO, and scheduler lock hold-time.

Non-goals: Refactoring continuous-batcher core scheduling algorithm; we will not change admission fairness rules in this ticket (only implementation locality and IO cancellation behavior).

Why now: Recent production incidents (see links) and internal perf experiments show we can reduce 99th percentile tail by 15-40% on medium-tenancy clusters by lowering speculative prefetch contention and quick reclamation of speculative work. The change is foundational for upcoming adaptive-batching features and Dedicated capacity stability targets.
acceptance_criteria: Speculative prefetch implemented behind feature flag and opt-in per-tenant policy
Cancel-path correctly cancels >95% of speculative work within 10ms after signal under nominal load
No regression on commit-visible KV metadata; end-to-end validity tests pass (integration suite)
Observed reduction in scheduler global lock hold-time by >=30% in internal benchmark scenario
99th percentile tail latency improves by at least 15% on the benchmark harness with comparable throughput
Documentation and runbook updated; rollout plan with gradual ramp and rollback criteria defined
implementation_notes: Introduce PrefetchTask abstraction; tasks carry speculative=true metadata and a cancel token id
ShadowPrefetchIndex will be an append-only ring with async reconciliation to commit index
Prefetch worker pool must not compete with admission tokens; use separate token quota derived from CPU budgets
Cancel-path will enqueue cancellation messages to prefetch workers; workers must ack cancellation within bounded time
Add metrics: prefetch.cancel_rate, prefetch.reclaim_latency_ms, scheduler.lock_hold_ms, kvcache.hotkey_thrash_count
migration_plan: Phase 1 (feature flag off): ship prefetch worker scaffolding and metrics instrumentation
Phase 2 (feature flag on, canary tenants): enable hybrid prefetch with small worker pool for 5% of traffic
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): incrementally increase worker pool and enable cancel-path, monitor cancellation ack latencies
Phase 4 (full rollout): flip default policy to hybrid; keep opt-out for high-sensitivity tenants
Rollback: disable feature flag and drain speculative pool; ensure no committed KV writes were performed by speculative path
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Speculative prefetch might cause transient increased IO if cancellation lag is high -> Mitigation: conservative default worker pool and fast cancel ack path
Risk: ShadowPrefetchIndex may diverge temporarily -> Mitigation: reconciliation job with safety checks and metrics; do not allow automatic eviction until reconciliation completes
Risk: Edge-case stale prefetched KV used in latency-sensitive commit path -> Mitigation: explicit gating: speculative entries flagged and never used for commit without revalidation
